summary.title: Extensible Scheduler Class
summary.one_liner: You learn how sched_ext lets a BPF program implement a custom Linux CPU scheduler with dispatch queues, safe fallback to the default scheduler, and debugging/monitoring hooks.
takeaways: sched_ext is a Linux scheduler class whose behavior is defined by BPF programs implementing struct sched_ext_ops, and only ops.name is mandatory.
The default scheduler is restored on error, on a stalled runnable task, or on SysRq-S, so system integrity is kept even if the BPF scheduler misbehaves.
Tasks are queued in dispatch queues (DSQs): a global FIFO, per-CPU local DSQs, and custom DSQs; a CPU runs from its local DSQ first.
Status can be checked via /sys/kernel/sched_ext/state, root/ops, enable_seq, per-scheduler events counters, and the drgn script scx_show_state.py.
summary.summary: This kernel documentation page describes sched_ext, a Linux scheduler class whose policy is written as BPF programs implementing struct sched_ext_ops. It covers how to enable it through kernel config options, how tasks are switched to it (including the SCX_OPS_SWITCH_PARTIAL flag), and how the scheduling cycle, dispatch queues, and ops.dequeue() custody rules work. It also walks through a minimal global FIFO example from scx_simple, lists the example schedulers under tools/sched_ext, and explains the sysfs/procfs status files, event counters, and bypass-mode module parameters. The page ends with a note that the APIs have no ABI stability guarantees.
